title: Cue Lifecycle — Playpad
content:
Purpose and quick note
----------------------
This is a personal playpad to track experiments around cue/template lifecycle: how prompts age, when to rotate few-shot exemplars, what signals should trigger a rollback, and lightweight heuristics for anchoring user context. Keeping it intentionally informal — misc notes, quick test outputs, TODOs.

High-level goals
- Define operational heuristics (cheap, signal-driven) for prompt rotation and rollback.
- Capture micro-failures that only show up in longitudinal usage (drift, anchoring bleed, exemplar staleness).
- Build small, reproducible few-shot permutations to use in A/B tests.

Why lifecycle matters (short)
- Prompts/templates are not static: product copy, policy, or user expectations change. A prompt that worked week 0 might degrade as user language shifts.
- Exemplars (few-shot in-context examples) can overfit to a transient corpus; need TTL/decay.
- Rollbacks must be low-friction: minimize config churn while avoiding extended regressions.

Key signals to monitor (cheap, approximate)
- Acceptance delta: sudden drop in rubric-acceptance rate vs baseline for a route (+10% relative).
- Latent semantics shift: embedding-centroid drift of recent prompts/queries > threshold.
- Output volatility spike: variance of top-3 token probs increases suddenly.
- User rollback actions: manual corrections or re-submissions recorded by frontend.

Experiment log excerpts (canonicalized)
2024-11-02 — initial anchor vs no-anchor test- test: same instruction with/without profile anchor ("You are a concise research assistant...")- result: anchor reduced hallucination on factual queries by ~8% but increased omission on open-ended prompts (users wanted exploratory answers)- note: anchors help when task is bounded; harm when user intent is exploratory

2024-12-04 — exemplar TTL probing- setup: 6 exemplars rotated every N days; tracked acceptance score on eval set- N=7: acceptance stable then sudden 6% drop after dataset drift event; N=14: marginally better but slower adaptation; N=3: brittle to small label noise- conclusion: hybrid approach: keep 2 stable exemplars + 2 rolling exemplars

2025-01-10 — prefix-caching interaction (serving/runtime)- observation: persistent prefix cache across sessions caused subtle persona bleed when using a single pinned route with multiple tenants in dev env (BUG filed: MLINF-712)- takeaway: invalidate prefix cache on route-metadata-change, consider session-scoped cache keys

Practical heuristics to try (notes)
- Exemplar set composition: 50% canonical (stable), 50% rotating (most recent high-quality user examples). Replace oldest rotating exemplar if acceptance < baseline for 3 consecutive checks.
- Anchor strength scaling: if task entropy (measured on historical outputs) > threshold, reduce anchor explicitness (shorter anchor).
- Decay schedule: exemplars tagged with creation_date + quality_score; perform weekly sweep to demote bottom quartile unless protected by manual pin.
- Rollback trigger: if route acceptance drops > 12% over 48 hours and secondary metric (user re-requests or higher error rate) also up, rollback to previous template within 1 hour and alert.

Sample prompts and few-shot packs (for quick copy/paste testing)
-- Template A (anchor + instruction) --
You are a concise, neutral domain assistant. Use short, factual sentences. If unsure, say "I don't know" and propose 2 plausible research steps.

Example 1: Q: "Summarize the main tradeoffs of quantization"
A: "Quantization reduces memory and compute by reducing precision; tradeoffs: accuracy loss at very low bits, need for calibration, potential latency improvements on specialized kernels. Next steps: test 8-bit on dev set; run calibration on representative samples."

Few-shot pack (4 exemplars) — rotating slot in index 3- exemplar-1 (stable): short definitional Q/A, high-quality canonical language- exemplar-2 (stable): short step-by-step diagnostic Q/A- exemplar-3 (rotating): recent user example (last week)- exemplar-4 (stable): fall-back redirection style (policy-safe answer)

Failure cases I've seen (concrete)
- Prompt anchoring creates fragile consensus: model locks on the anchor and refuses to consider clarified follow-ups. Fix attempted: allow explicit counter-instruction in follow-ups ("Ignore previous anchor for this follow-up").
- Exemplars with too much context cause the model to mimic the example structure even when irrelevant (copycat-structure). Solution to try: reduce exemplar verbosity and add explicit comment line: "Format only, not content".
- TTL too long leads to concept drift (exemplar references outdated product names). Micro-mitigation: quick regex-scan sweep to find stale keywords tied to product release tags.

Quick checks / regression micro-tests (manual)
- Sanity-check suite (10 queries) to run daily: 3 factual, 3 exploratory, 2 procedural, 2 policy-sensitive. Log: date, route, exemplar-ids, acceptance.- If acceptance decreased and embedding-centroid drifted > 0.07, escalate.

Open questions / hypotheses (to validate)
- H1: Two-tier exemplar lists (stable + rolling) provide most robustness across drift events vs equal-weight rotation.- H2: Anchors should be dynamically shortened when user query length > 120 tokens; otherwise they dominate.- H3: Automatic rollback based solely on single metric is noisy — needs composite signal (acceptance + frontend re-do ratio + embedding shift).

To-dos (short)
- [ ] Script to tag exemplars with quality_score (quick rule: acceptance rate * recency-weight) — prototype by Jan 24- [ ] Add prefix-cache invalidation test in serving sandbox (linked PR draft) — WIP- [ ] Build 10-question sanity suite and wire into daily smoke job- [ ] Schedule 30-min sync with Maya and Lucas to review exemplar rotation proposal (date: 2025-01-22 suggested)

Notes to self (voice)
- Keep experiments small and reproducible. Capture exact exemplar ids and prompt text for every run.- Favor metrics that correlate with end-user behavior (re-requests, edits) over purely internal perplexity.- When a rollback helps, record why (was it exemplar staleness, policy change, or model update?) — we need provenance to avoid oscillation.

Scratch ideas (quick)
- 'age-weighted retrieval' for few-shot: when constructing context, sample exemplars weighted by both quality and recency with a temperature parameter.- 'anchor attenuation' operator: progressively strip sentences from anchor during generation for exploratory prompts.

End of playpad — overwrite freely. If something stabilizes, move to prompt-library index and write a short blurb for console (why we pinned this pack).
